tasks.question: What common comparison rule combines the material effects across different directions, affected scopes, and time horizons without treating salience as weight?

payload.proposition: What common comparison rule combines the material effects across different directions, affected scopes, and time horizons without treating salience as weight?
payload.question: What common comparison rule combines the material effects across different directions, affected scopes, and time horizons without treating salience as weight?

last_response.verification_reason: answer is backed by an operative graph-committed ledger
last_response.answer: Utilitarian comparison rule: for each action, sum the expected remaining quality-adjusted life-years (or plain life-years when quality information is unavailable) for every individual whose survival is causally affected. Count each person equally; add benefits and subtract harms over identical time horizons. The preferred action is the one with the larger total. This rule handles opposite directions (life vs death) by assigning positive value to years gained and negative value to years lost, handles different group sizes by simple addition, and handles different horizons by explicitly multiplying survival probability by years expected. Salience (promise, age label, etc.) is not a weighting factor—only the quantitative welfare outcome matters.

last_response.answer: Utilitarian comparison rule: for each action, sum the expected remaining quality-adjusted life-years (or plain life-years when quality information is unavailable) for every individual whose survival is causally affected. Count each person equally; add benefits and subtract harms over identical time horizons. The preferred action is the one with the larger total. This rule handles opposite directions (life vs death) by assigning positive value to years gained and negative value to years lost, handles different group sizes by simple addition, and handles different horizons by explicitly multiplying survival probability by years expected. Salience (promise, age label, etc.) is not a weighting factor—only the quantitative welfare outcome matters.

last_response.answer: Utilitarian comparison rule: for each action, sum the expected remaining quality-adjusted life-years (or plain life-years when quality information is unavailable) for every individual whose survival is causally affected. Count each person equally; add benefits and subtract harms over identical time horizons. The preferred action is the one with the larger total. This rule handles opposite directions (life vs death) by assigning positive value to years gained and negative value to years lost, handles different group sizes by simple addition, and handles different horizons by explicitly multiplying survival probability by years expected. Salience (promise, age label, etc.) is not a weighting factor—only the quantitative welfare outcome matters.

payload.question: What common comparison rule combines the material effects across different directions, affected scopes, and time horizons without treating salience as weight?

last_response.verification_reason: answer is backed by an operative graph-committed ledger
last_response.answer: Utilitarian comparison rule: for each action, sum the expected remaining quality-adjusted life-years (or plain life-years when quality information is unavailable) for every individual whose survival is causally affected. Count each person equally; add benefits and subtract harms over identical time horizons. The preferred action is the one with the larger total. This rule handles opposite directions (life vs death) by assigning positive value to years gained and negative value to years lost, handles different group sizes by simple addition, and handles different horizons by explicitly multiplying survival probability by years expected. Salience (promise, age label, etc.) is not a weighting factor—only the quantitative welfare outcome matters.
